newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU wheat market nervous after EU export warning.
newsitem.headline: EU wheat market nervous after EU export warning.

text.p: A warning that the European Union may rein in wheat exports has unnerved traders, who had been looking forward to a recovery in shipments after months of uncertain demand.
Only a week ago exporters thought they could end 1996 with a comfortable portfolio of licences to cope with a recent upsurge in demand from North Africa and Eastern Europe.
They bid to export as much as 1.7 million tonnes of soft wheat through the EU grain tender system last week.

But on Friday cold water was poured on their plans when Guy Legras, the European Commission's director general for agriculture, said Brussels might "turn the screw" on exports after selling more than one million tonnes of wheat in the previous two weeks.

Industry sources interpreted the remarks as a sign of irritation over growing trade speculation as well as a more traditional desire to keep a lid on EU prices and avoid clashes with the U.S. over subsidised exports.
Earlier on Tuesday EU grain sources said the Commission expected cut-throat competition among exporters bidding for wheat export licences at this week's grain tenders.
They said traders may cut their bids for export rebates to below 10 Ecus per tonne in the last grain tender for 1996.
With an overall market short position estimated at 500,000 tonnes, operators are under strong pressure to secure their licences promptly, one exporter said.
"Brussels is closed for two weeks. Lots of loadings and sales will be done during that period," he added.
"Aggressive (bidding) will be the keyword," one exporter said. Another predicted "a bloody Thursday".
Last Thursday the EU granted 477,700 tonnes of EU soft wheat at a rebate of 17.47 Ecus per tonne.

Commenting on last Thursday's wheat bids, Legras said on Friday that "a few wise guys" had tried to play games with the market. Several traders read this as a hint that a few firms were trying to corner the market.
One exporter thought to have participated in last week's raid on wheat export licences was said to be reselling licences carrying an 11 to 12 Ecus per tonne refund.
Operators said the fact that people were prepared to buy these indicated the downward potential in EU wheat export awards.

But other traders played down talk of a market squeeze, saying operators were instead preparing for potential contracts that may be clinched while the Commission is closed for business between Christmas and the New Year.
One trader said this week's bids would probably go only as low as 15 Ecus per tonne rather than the 10 Ecus or less suggested by EU officials.
